title: Margraviate of Brandenburg
capsule: The Margraviate of Brandenburg was a March of the Holy Roman Empire created in 1157 when Albert the Bear, Margrave of the Northern March, captured the castle of Brandenburg from Jaxa of Köpenick and consolidated Ascanian rule over the region between the Elbe and Oder rivers. It became one of seven imperial electorates under the Golden Bull of 1356, giving its ruler a permanent voice in electing the Holy Roman Emperor. After the extinction of the Ascanian line (1320) and subsequent Wittelbach and Luxembourg tenures, Hohenzollern Burgrave Frederick VI of Nuremberg received the margraviate from Emperor Sigismund in 1411 and was formally invested as Margrave Frederick I at the Council of Constance in 1415, establishing the dynasty that would rule until 1918.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Brandenburg's boundaries are well-documented in imperial records and diplomatic instruments from the thirteenth century onward; earlier Ascanian territorial claims eastward are less precisely delimited.
